entries.hypotheses_domain: Complex circulant C=p(S), n>=1, Sx_j=x_(j+1), omega=exp(2pi i/n); no simplicity or nonzero-eigenvalue assumption.
entries.claim:
\begin{theorem}[eigenvalues of circulants]\label{linear:thm:circulant}
For $a\in\Z/n$ let $v_a=(\omega^{aj})_{j\in\Z/n}$. Then $Cv_a=p(\omega^a)v_a$ for every circulant $C=p(S)$. The vectors
$v_a/\sqrt n$ form an orthonormal basis of $\C^n$, so every circulant is normal, and
\[
\det C=\prod_{a=0}^{n-1}p(\omega^a).
\]
\end{theorem}
entries.earlier_tools_and_proof_sites: Actually read C11 Hermitian50-118/matrix-unit orthogonality293-368/regular multiplicity397-443; local earlier circulant theorem, commutant, character basis, Paley spectrum, Delsarte and Plotkin complete proofs in this appendix reread in printed order. Earlier C6 multivariable UFD619-787, C7 Jordan828-905, V1 sequence/BW and linear-algebra proof sites as APPB-REVIEW; no later-volume premise.
entries.reconstruction_A: For each a, the wrapped shift gives Sv_a=omega^a v_a since omega^(an)=1. Polynomial evaluation yields Cv_a=p(omega^a)v_a. With the declared linear-first Hermitian product, the inner product is sum_j omega^((a-b)j): zero for a!=b by a finite geometric sum with nonzero denominator, and n for a=b. Thus U=(v_a/sqrt(n)) is unitary and U*CU=D. Compute CC*=UDD*U*=UD*DU*=C*C; determinants of U and U* cancel, giving product p(omega^a).
entries.adversarial_check_B: Independent inverse reconstruction, not the eigenvector argument: (UDU*)_jk=(1/n) sum_a sum_r c_r omega^(a(r+j-k)). Sum first in a; only r=k-j modulo n survives, giving c_(k-j), exactly the original matrix entry. This reconstructs every entry even with repeated eigenvalues or a singular matrix. Normality and determinant then follow directly from this factorization.
entries.boundary_probes: n=1 gives the one scalar and unit basis; C=0 and scalar C for n>=2 have many eigenvectors outside the selected basis, so the former claim all the eigenvectors was literally false. Coincident p-values, complex nonsymmetric coefficients and determinant zero require no division by p(omega^a). Only a!=b divides 1-omega^(a-b).
entries.defects_and_corrections: Changed the proof wording from all the eigenvectors to these vectors form a basis. The original theorem is retained in full, including normality and determinant; no weaker replacement.

entries.hypotheses_domain: Complex n-by-n circulants, n>=1; inverse assertion only for invertible C; t in C with t^n!=1.
entries.earlier_tools_and_proof_sites: Actually read C11 Hermitian50-118/matrix-unit orthogonality293-368/regular multiplicity397-443; local earlier circulant theorem, commutant, character basis, Paley spectrum, Delsarte and Plotkin complete proofs in this appendix reread in printed order. Earlier C6 multivariable UFD619-787, C7 Jordan828-905, V1 sequence/BW and linear-algebra proof sites as APPB-REVIEW; no later-volume premise.
entries.reconstruction_A: I,S,...,S^(n-1) have distinct unit positions in the first row and span circulants, so dimension n. Products reduce modulo S^n=I and commute. S*=S^-1 gives adjoint closure, including conjugation of coefficients. For an invertible circulant its eigenvalues p(omega^a) are nonzero. Lagrange interpolation at the n distinct roots of unity gives q(omega^a)=1/p(omega^a), hence q(S)C=Cq(S)=I. Multiplying the finite geometric polynomial on both sides gives (I-tS)^-1=(sum_(j=0)^(n-1)t^j S^j)/(1-t^n).
entries.adversarial_check_B: Compare the entire actual answer: its distinct inverse proof starts CS=SC and multiplies by C^-1 to get C^-1 S=S C^-1; the earlier commutant proposition then gives a circulant inverse. This agrees with interpolation and avoids invoking Cayley-Hamilton. Direct multiplication on both sides verifies the requested geometric inverse. Zero C demonstrates why inverse closure needs its explicit invertibility qualifier.
entries.boundary_probes: n=1, t=0, singular C and arbitrary complex coefficients; t^n=1 is excluded and indeed makes I-tS singular since t^-1 is a shift eigenvalue.
entries.defects_and_corrections: Made invertible explicit in the prompt and defined matrix algebra before use. All original intended conclusions and the complete supplied solution retained.

entries.hypotheses_domain: Binary character matrix H_n indexed by words/subsets of length n>=0; H_0=[1]; block recursion only n>=1; count scalar additions/subtractions.
entries.earlier_tools_and_proof_sites: Actually read C11 Hermitian50-118/matrix-unit orthogonality293-368/regular multiplicity397-443; local earlier circulant theorem, commutant, character basis, Paley spectrum, Delsarte and Plotkin complete proofs in this appendix reread in printed order. Earlier C6 multivariable UFD619-787, C7 Jordan828-905, V1 sequence/BW and linear-algebra proof sites as APPB-REVIEW; no later-volume premise.
entries.reconstruction_A: For n>=1 write word and character index as first bit and remaining n-1 bits. (-1)^(t1*x1) supplies the four block signs, so H_n=[[H,H],[H,-H]]. Apply H to u+v and u-v. Each of 2^(n-1) paired positions uses two scalar operations, hence T(n)=2T(n-1)+2^n. H_0 returns its sole input with T(0)=0. Divide by 2^n and induct to obtain T(n)=n2^n for every n>=0.
entries.adversarial_check_B: Reverse the butterfly order: first recursively transform u and v, then add/subtract outputs; linearity gives the identical block action. Independently dense character sums using parity of bitwise intersection match the recursive transform for n=0..6, with exact cost n2^n. This finite computation supports the character factorization and induction, not replaces them.
entries.boundary_probes: n=0 has a singleton empty word/character, matrix [1], no H_-1 and no arithmetic. n=1 is the explicit 2-by-2 butterfly. The block symbol is defined locally; no general tensor product theory or bit-complexity claim is needed.
entries.defects_and_corrections: Genuine boundary gap: the old standing n>=0 domain reached H_(n-1) and F2^(n-1) at n=0. Added H_0 base, n>=1 restrictions to main recursion/prompt/solution and zero-cost base. Retained the algorithm and exact operation count on the entire intended domain.

entries.hypotheses_domain: p prime, p=1 modulo4, nonzero nonsquare c in F_p; graph on F_p with nonzero square differences, distinct vertices only.
entries.earlier_tools_and_proof_sites: Actually read C11 Hermitian50-118/matrix-unit orthogonality293-368/regular multiplicity397-443; local earlier circulant theorem, commutant, character basis, Paley spectrum, Delsarte and Plotkin complete proofs in this appendix reread in printed order. entries.reconstruction_A: The nonzero squares form an index-two subgroup S; cS is its other coset. Multiplication by c is bijective and swaps S and cS, so it exchanges adjacency and nonadjacency for all distinct vertices. Since -1 is a square, the graph is undirected. With P e_x=e_(cx), relabeling gives P A P^-1=J-I-A; similarity preserves the characteristic polynomial and all multiplicities.
entries.adversarial_check_B: Use the earlier character eigenbasis directly: J-I-A acts on constants by p-1-(p-1)/2=(p-1)/2 and on each nonconstant character by -1-lambda. This exchanges (-1+sqrt(p))/2 and (-1-sqrt(p))/2 with equal multiplicities (p-1)/2, independently checking the complete spectrum. On entries, (PAP^-1)_(cx,cy)=A_(x,y), exactly the complement at (cx,cy).
entries.boundary_probes: p>=5. Zero differences are excluded; c is invertible. Over composite residue rings nonzero nonunits invalidate the two-coset argument, so prime is explicit, as already required by the definition of P_p. The old inverse-conjugation formula is ALSO true here because c^-1 is nonsquare; this is a convention clarification, not a spurious mathematical defect.
entries.defects_and_corrections: Made prime explicit in the prompt and specified P e_x=e_phi(x) before PAP^-1. Original P_p prime-field target and full spectrum retained.

entries.hypotheses_domain: Prime-field Paley graph P_17; prove clique number3 and the finite Ramsey lower bound R(4,4)>=18, not an exact Ramsey upper bound.
entries.earlier_tools_and_proof_sites: Actually read C11 Hermitian50-118/matrix-unit orthogonality293-368/regular multiplicity397-443; local earlier circulant theorem, commutant, character basis, Paley spectrum, Delsarte and Plotkin complete proofs in this appendix reread in printed order. Earlier C6 multivariable UFD619-787, C7 Jordan828-905, V1 sequence/BW and linear-algebra proof sites as APPB-REVIEW; no later-volume premise.
entries.reconstruction_A: Squares are {1,2,4,8,9,13,15,16}. Normalize any edge (x,y) to (0,1) by (z-x)/(y-x); its denominator is a nonzero square. Common neighbors are exactly {2,9,16}; their pair differences are 7,14,7, all nonsquares, so a 4-clique is impossible. Triangle {0,1,2} exists. The preceding self-complementarity gives no independent 4-set; color K_17 by edges/nonedges to obtain R(4,4)>=18. Existence of finite Ramsey numbers is proved by induction from R(1,b)=R(a,1)=1 using the neighborhood recurrence for a,b>=2.
entries.adversarial_check_B: Exact independent enumeration of all triples and all 2380 quadruples gives 68 triangles and no 4-clique in either color. The general proof is the affine reduction, not this enumeration. Reconstruct recurrence: on N=R(a-1,b)+R(a,b-1) vertices, if both incident color degrees were below their thresholds, their sum would be <=N-2 rather than N-1. The relevant neighborhood gives the smaller clique or a clique to extend at the chosen vertex. Induction terminates at a=1 or b=1.
entries.boundary_probes: The sqrt(17) bound alone only gives clique number <=4, so it cannot exclude 4. R(0,b) is undefined and not used: recurrence explicitly a,b>=2. The lower bound is not a claim R(4,4)=18. Corrected a prior reviewer-record typo saying differences3/10; actual source and the recomputation give7/14.
entries.defects_and_corrections: Restricted the general Ramsey recurrence to a,b>=2. Original clique number, explicit coloring and Ramsey lower-bound targets retained; no loss.

entries.hypotheses_domain: All binary codes C subset {0,1}^8, including empty, with pairwise distances at least4; prove A(8,4)=16 using k=1,2 Delsarte and an attaining code.
entries.earlier_tools_and_proof_sites: Actually read C11 Hermitian50-118/matrix-unit orthogonality293-368/regular multiplicity397-443; local earlier circulant theorem, commutant, character basis, Paley spectrum, Delsarte and Plotkin complete proofs in this appendix reread in printed order. Earlier C6 multivariable UFD619-787, C7 Jordan828-905, V1 sequence/BW and linear-algebra proof sites as APPB-REVIEW; no later-volume premise.
entries.reconstruction_A: If C is empty its size is already <=16. Otherwise M>0, define the average distance distribution a_i, a0=1,a1=a2=a3=0, and M=1+sum_(i=4)^8 a_i. The k1 inequality is 2a5+4a6+6a7+8a8<=8. The k2 values at 0,4,5,6,7,8 are28,-4,-2,4,14,28. Add one quarter of the rearranged k2 inequality to k1 to get a4+2.5a5+3a6+2.5a7+a8<=15; all coefficients>=1, yielding M<=16. For attainment evaluate every affine F2^3 function a0+sum ai xi. f(0) and f(e_i)+f(0) recover all four coefficients, so there are 16 distinct words. A nonconstant affine difference is balanced by a translation where its linear part is1, giving weight4; constant1 gives8. The difference x1 attains weight4, giving minimum distance exactly4.
entries.adversarial_check_B: Independent polynomial certificate f(t)=(t-4)(t-8)=2K0(t)+2K1(t)+K2(t)/2. It is <=0 at every allowed nonzero distance4..8 and f(0)=32. Delsarte gives sum a_i f(i)>=2M while the sign condition gives <=32, so M<=16. A second upper check keeps at least half of a code at one fixed coordinate and deletes it; earlier Plotkin(7,4) bounds that half by8. Exact all120 pair distances in the 16-word affine construction confirm the weight proof; each word has14 neighbors at4 and one at8.
entries.boundary_probes: The average distribution is not defined for an empty code; the explicit empty guard now precedes it. Singleton codes have a0=1 and all other a_i=0. The two nonzero-distance types are earned, and coefficient recovery proves distinctness rather than assuming 16 coefficient tuples give 16 words. No LP duality theorem is imported.
entries.defects_and_corrections: Genuine gap: old solution averaged over choices in C without handling C empty. Added the empty case and explicit coefficient-recovery proof for the lower construction. Retained exactly A(8,4)=16, the prescribed k1/k2 route and full reader-facing solution.
